questions.title: What is the physical interpretation of the rescale factor $\lambda_i$ in the unified RoPE equation?
questions.question_body: In Section 2.1, the paper defines the unified positional interpolation formula (Eq. 2) where the rotation angle is scaled by $\lambda(\beta)^i$. I understand that $\lambda$ relates to the extension ratio $s$, but I am struggling to visualize what changing $\lambda_i$ actually does to the geometry of the attention mechanism. Does a larger $\lambda_i$ effectively 'slow down' the rotation for that specific dimension, allowing it to cover a longer sequence before repeating? How does this relate to the concept of 'crowded' positions mentioned in the Linear PI discussion?

questions.title: Why is the monotonicity constraint $\lambda_i \le \lambda_{i+1}$ justified by NTK theory?
questions.question_body: In Section 3.2, under 'Monotonically non-decreasing constraint', the authors state that they enforce $\lambda_i \le \lambda_{i+1}$ based on NTK theory. The text says this implies lower dimensions (higher frequency) require less interpolation. However, intuitively, wouldn't higher frequency components (lower $i$) be more sensitive to changes and thus require *more* careful handling or potentially different scaling than low frequency ones? Could someone explain the specific link between the Neural Tangent Kernel perspective and why the rescale factors must increase monotonically with the dimension index $i$?

questions.title: How exactly does the 'progressive extension' avoid catastrophic forgetting without direct 2048k training data?
questions.question_body: The abstract and Section 3.3 describe a progressive strategy: search for 256k -> fine-tune at 256k -> search again on the fine-tuned model to reach 2048k. My confusion lies in the second search step. If the model was only fine-tuned on sequences up to 256k tokens, how does performing a new evolutionary search for rescale factors allow it to suddenly generalize to 2048k tokens (an 8x jump from its training limit) without seeing any actual text of that length during gradient updates? Is the claim that the 'non-uniform interpolation' found by the search is so robust that it acts as a perfect zero-shot extrapolator once the model has adapted to intermediate lengths?

questions.title: Clarification on the indicator function $\mathbb{I}(\hat{\lambda}_{i}, \hat{n})$ for initial tokens
questions.question_body: In Equation 3, the rescaling factor is defined piecewise: it equals 1 (no change) for $n < \hat{n}$ and $1/\lambda_i$ for $n \ge \hat{n}$. Finding 2 states that initial tokens should undergo less interpolation. If $\hat{n}$ is set to, say, 32, does this mean the first 32 tokens retain their original absolute positional encodings regardless of whether the total sequence length is 8k or 2048k? If so, doesn't this create a discontinuity in relative positions between token 31 and token 32 when the sequence gets very long, potentially confusing the attention heads?

questions.title: Why does Mistral perform better with 128k fine-tuning while LLaMA2 prefers 256k for the final 2048k extension?
questions.question_body: In Section 4.2 ('Long sequence language modeling beyond 2000k'), there is an interesting divergence: LLaMA2 achieves better perplexity at 2048k when fine-tuned at 256k, whereas Mistral performs better when fine-tuned at only 128k. The authors attribute Mistral's behavior to using a fixed 16k training length during fine-tuning (following YaRN settings). Can someone elaborate on why training on shorter chunks (16k) would make a model *better* suited for extreme extrapolation via search compared to training on longer chunks? Usually, one would expect training on lengths closer to the target to yield better results.

questions.title: Is the computational cost of the evolutionary search feasible for custom models?
questions.question_body: The paper mentions searching over a space of size roughly $4 \times 10^{167}$ for a modest extension, using an evolutionary algorithm with population size $P=64$ and computing perplexity on sample batches. While they claim efficiency, calculating perplexity even on small batches for a 7B parameter model is expensive. For a researcher wanting to apply LongRoPE to a new architecture or a different base length (not just replicating their exact setup), is this search process tractable on consumer hardware or single-GPU setups, or does it inherently require multi-node clusters similar to their fine-tuning setup (8-16 A100s)?
